name: Recovery sauna
rationale: Circulation, stiffness, sleep and the simple fact that you enjoy it. No performance claim attached — this one is for feeling human.
how_to: Go in warm, after training rather than before
15–20 min is plenty; this is not the adaptation session
Cool down gradually, then drink to your post-weight

name: Heat-acclimation session
rationale: The dose that actually expands plasma volume. Straight after a run, while core temperature is already up — that is the protocol the research used, and it is far more time-efficient than heating from cold.
how_to: Within ~10 min of finishing the run, before you cool off
Build to 25–30 min across the first week — do not open at full dose
Sit low for the first sessions if the top bench is too much
Weigh in and out. Every session.

name: Post-run top-up
rationale: Short exposure that keeps some heat stimulus ticking over between blocks without adding meaningful fatigue.
how_to: Short and easy — leave before it becomes work
Skip it entirely on a heavy training week

name: Post-lift sauna
rationale: Optional and low-stakes. Heat after lifting does not blunt strength adaptation the way cold-water immersion does, so if you like it, have it.
how_to: After the session, never between sets
Keep it short on heavy lower days — you still have to run tomorrow
